title: Phase 1 — clean checkout to isolated Dev VM, Little Mester response and rootless Docker smoke
objective: Child of #49; depends on evidence spike #50 (resolved after Sol review). Luna owns implementation; Sol owns architecture/review/completion. Deliver ONLY clean checkout → host-authorised single-workspace Dev VM → actual Little Mester model response → successful guest rootless Docker container. Full binding locked D1–D10, execution rules, external review protocol and exact handoff schema are in #49 and incorporated here. No Test VM, snapshots, self-test grant, recursion, metrics/auth migration or automatic Dev refresh implementation. All self-test authority remains absent/default-denied. Pushes exclusively by end user. Preserve current VM and old branches.

acceptance_criteria.text: Dedicated host-installed lifecycle MCP entrypoint, selected by the binary spawned, never ordinary-server env/arg/config switches. It and CLI use one trusted host core outside guest writes. Refuse absent host-owned installation provenance. Owner-controlled host process and private stdio pipes exclusively establish authority; no guest agent access. Ordinary-agent MCP neither registers nor dispatches lifecycle tools, including direct tools/call under hostile env/args/config. Guest source/config/flags cannot grant host resource authority. Never run trusted launcher/core/dependencies from agent-editable workspace. Explicitly reviewed initial candidate may run under owner control outside export; installation/update remains owner-only.

Exactly one canonical host-selected workspace is exported; reject unsafe paths/symlinks/substitution and do not share host policy, state, credentials, other workspaces or Docker socket. Policy code and runtime state outside export. No sourcing mutable workspace .little-mester.conf in trusted execution. No arbitrary workspace-selected executable/host shell command facility in MCP.

Reuse v1 guest rootless Docker installation and direct guest agent startup; disable system rootful Docker and verify user daemon SecurityOptions includes name=rootless. Preserve restrict=on and proven public HTTP(S) mediation with host/private/LAN denial; no direct host/LAN route or additional published ports beyond loopback control. One working model provider only; private owner-managed credential provisioning, never ticket/log credentials.

Startup has bounded prerequisite/download/boot/readiness/agent checks; visible v1-style stage logs plus bounded v2-style diagnostic retention and cleanup only of positively identified run-owned processes. Missing KVM, terminal bootstrap failure, timeout and ambiguous process ownership fail safely without deleting valuable/unrelated state. No nested virtualisation.

In an owner-authorised clean host checkout, launch a NEW isolated Dev VM without altering current runtime; Little Mester returns a real response to a fixed non-secret prompt with the chosen provider. MCP handshake/help/version alone is NOT this acceptance. Record exact command, SHA, output, exit code and logs.

Inside that same Dev VM, a harmless Docker container actually executes and exits 0 using the guest rootless daemon; record exact command/image identity/output/exit and rootless evidence. docker info, pull/build or a mock alone is NOT container acceptance.

Focused local tests cover shared CLI/MCP policy parity, forged identity/config/env denial, guest lifecycle/default self-test denial, workspace escape/substitution, state/code outside export, rootless cloud-init generation, no host socket/network escape, bounded failure and ownership-safe cleanup. Existing ticket-engine MCP and host-Docker mode regressions pass; local/mocked results remain distinct from host acceptance.

ONE owner-run acceptance contract: ./lab-vm smoke --workspace "$V3_SMOKE_WORKSPACE" --credentials-file "$V3_PROVIDER_CREDENTIALS" from explicitly owner-reviewed candidate outside exported workspace (eventual trusted installed copy likewise protected). Implement this exact command; NOT_RUN until human executes after Sol diff/test review. Expected real stage proofs VM_UP, actual provider response VM_RESPONSE_OK, ROOTLESS_DOCKER_OK and actual completed container output DOCKER_CONTAINER_OK, exit 0; propagate every failure nonzero. Local unit/bats do not prove this gate. Missing owner prerequisites become NEEDS_HUMAN with this exact repo command and missing input, not open-ended discovery. Evidence before commits; no auto push/merge/refresh.

Executed stdio integration evidence: ordinary-server tools/list excludes lifecycle tools under hostile env/args/workspace config; direct tools/call lifecycle is rejected; dedicated host entrypoint refuses absent provenance; guest config/mounts/network expose neither host lifecycle process nor stdio/endpoint. Tests prove resource/transport isolation, not merely hidden tool names or a mode flag. Future guest self-testing authentication remains out of scope.

ORDER 1 SECURITY BLOCKER — source inspection of little-mester-mcp/src/mcp-server.ts shows one StdioServerTransport (line 554) connected to the MCP server (555), with no per-request authenticated host-human identity or authorization context. Its registered tools receive MCP arguments; client identity metadata is not an authenticated authority. Therefore, if the host-installed MCP tool is exposed to an ordinary agent, that agent can invoke any lifecycle tool under the same host process identity. This conflicts with #49 D4/#51 A1 ordinary-agent denial and the requirement that authority come from trusted host/transport binding, not tool arguments. A caller-supplied role/token or env flag would not solve it. Stop before tests/code; do not implement an MCP lifecycle path until Sol/user chooses an already-approved, independently authenticated transport/authority boundary or narrows MCP lifecycle access.

Order 1 findings and command matrix are in prior sequence-7 ledger entries. Decision boundary recorded first in docs/tickets/architecture/DECISIONS.md §L. No tests or implementation run.
